name: Write Changes
covers_text: Running python3 gmail_reader.py --mock --accounts fixtures/accounts.csv --name "Test Person" --count 5 --out latest.txt --rules rules.json writes latest.txt with permission 600, a header (mailbox, fetch time, count), 5 numbered emails newest first (date | from | subject, snippet on the next line), and a 'Most critical' section naming the email and matched words from rules.json
The code contains no send, delete, trash, modify or insert calls to Gmail, and the only scope used anywhere is https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly
README.md explains the admin setup (service account, domain-wide delegation, gmail.readonly only) and gives the exact live commands: dry run first, then fetch

gmail_reader.py implements the key handling, mailbox choice (--mailbox, or --accounts/GMAIL_READER_ACCOUNTS plus --name with CSV columns detected from the header), --count default 5 and max 50, --dry-run (prints actual address and message count, reads no emails), and one-line errors for missing key, bad key, unauthorized_client and mailbox not found, without ever printing the key; fixtures/inbox.json holds 10 made-up emails at example.test with fake names
purpose: gmail_reader.py, rules.json, requirements.txt, both fixtures and README.md do not exist.

envelope.stop_loss: Stop if spend reaches 400 or 25 calls, or if the mock command still fails after 2 retries, or if grep finds any send/delete/trash/modify/insert call.

completion_check: The mock command writes latest.txt with permission 600, grep finds no send/delete/trash/modify/insert calls, and README holds the admin setup and dry-run-then-fetch commands.

atoms.goal: The tool, rules, fixtures, requirements and README are built in the working folder and listed under Changes.
